ca_corona_dos_equis_wall.blurb: Corona/Dos Equis Wall lies on the west side of the Indian Cove campground area in Joshua Tree National Park. Dos Equis is a tall, steep, dark-brown face with long, exposed trad lines, while the smaller Corona Wall farther up the gully has shorter and somewhat gentler climbs. Of the 13 routes, nearly all are trad, from 5.7 up to a single 5.12, with most sitting in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. The rock is monzogranite. Walk-ins are brief, about five to fifteen minutes, with the South Buttress right by the road and everything else up the gully on the left side of the formation. A single-rope rappel from the top of Tecate gets you back down.

ca_4_cannibals_gully.blurb: Cannibals Gully is a shaded corner of the Snowshed Wall's east face at Donner Summit, along the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe. The gully looks north, catches very little sun and funnels wind, which makes it a welcome refuge when the rest of the summit is hot. Its 13 routes are mostly sport with a few trad lines on granodiorite, and the grades run steep: six are 5.13, a few are 5.12 and lower 5.10 to 5.11, and just one is 5.9. Only two distinct sport lines climb the wall, so lines of climbers form easily, and linking the routes together is popular.

ca_bong_aka_2001_the.blurb: The Bong, also known as 2001, is a freestanding 75-foot monolith in the Lake Arrowhead Pinnacles of the San Bernardino Mountains, with no easy way to its top. Routes wrap around most sides of it, the west face being the standout, and many carry space-flavored names. Of the 13 routes, 11 are sport and two are trad; seven are 5.11, three reach 5.12, and the rest are a couple of 5.9s and a lone 5.10, which makes it the place in the Pinnacles for leading 5.11. The rock is monzogranite. Expect a long uphill hike of an hour or more on a brushy path that ends at a fairly level base.

ca_bootjack_boulders.blurb: Bootjack Boulders is a small bouldering patch on Mount Tamalpais, in Mount Tamalpais State Park off Panoramic Highway in Marin. It holds 13 problems on serpentinite, running from about V2 into the V5 range, with five of them at the harder end and the rest moderate. Aretes and sit-start variations are the common themes. A faint trail of roughly 150 feet leads up from the road to the blocks, so the area suits a short session or a stop while exploring the mountain rather than a big day out.
